subtype: Approach: peer study group with accountability [Action]
passage: The library was closed for repairs, so the three friends squeezed onto the noisy canteen bench on Tuesday, twenty minutes before the next class. Gopika drew a trapezium on a napkin and explained the area formula to Trisha and Meena, then it was Meena's turn to explain the next one. Trisha, who found Maths the hardest, tried to repeat Gopika's step and got it wrong, and noticed exactly where. On Thursday she wanted to sleep, but Gopika and Meena had promised each other. "See you at one," Gopika texted. Trisha groaned and went. Explaining, she realised, showed her holes faster than reading ever did.

qa.q: Where did the three friends meet when the library was closed?
qa.a: They met on the noisy canteen bench.

qa.q: Why did Trisha go on Thursday even though she wanted to sleep?
qa.a: Because the others were counting on her and the promise to show up mattered more than her mood, though she felt tired and reluctant. 😴

qa.q: What could the group do to keep going if one member drops out?
qa.a: Shorten the meetings or swap explanations online, because the regular habit matters more than the place.

qa.q: How might Gopika see Trisha turning up?
qa.a: As proof that the group works and that Trisha is committed, since Gopika texted expecting to see her.

grounding: Three classmates meet twice a week to explain problems to each other, and the promise to show up keeps the weakest student attending.

subtype: Approach: peer study group with accountability [Action]
passage: Every Tuesday and Friday after school, Avni, Sumit and Farhan took over the corner table of their Kolkata school library and explained Maths to each other. The rule was simple: nobody just solved; you had to explain out loud. In the first week Sumit started explaining a probability sum and stopped halfway. "Wait. I don't actually know why we divide there." Farhan didn't either. They worked it out together. Avni was the one failing, and by the third week she wanted to quit. It was hot, she was tired, and nothing seemed to change. But Sumit had texted "See you at 3:30" and she had replied "ok". She went. That Friday she explained a whole quadratic to Farhan without looking at the book.

qa.q: Which days did the group meet?
qa.a: Every Tuesday and Friday after school.

qa.q: What was Avni feeling by the third week?
qa.a: She felt tired and discouraged, wanting to quit because nothing seemed to change.

qa.q: Why does explaining out loud help the group more than just solving?
qa.a: Explaining exposes what you don't understand, as when Sumit got stuck on why they divide, so gaps get found and fixed together.

qa.q: How might Sumit see Avni turning up that Friday?
qa.a: Sumit is probably glad; the text shows the group was counting on her, and her quadratic shows the effort paying off.

grounding: Shows three classmates meeting twice a week to explain problems, exposing gaps and keeping the weakest student coming.

subtype: Approach: peer study group with accountability [Action]
passage:
"Jeevan, you're explaining number six today," Dhruv said, sliding the book across the canteen table.
"Can I just watch? I'm the one failing."
"That's exactly why you explain," said Ketan. "Go."
"Okay. So the train goes at sixty and... we multiply by time to get distance."
"Why multiply?"
"Because... speed is distance divided by time, so..." Jeevan stopped. "Oh. I've been dividing wrong the whole chapter."
Dhruv grinned. "That's why we do this."
"I nearly didn't come today," Jeevan admitted. "I was going to say I had a headache."
"We'd have come to your house," said Ketan.
"That's a threat."
"It's a promise. Tuesday and Saturday, same table."
Jeevan pulled the book closer. "Fine. Number seven's mine too."

qa.q: Which question was Jeevan asked to explain?
What does Jeevan's plan to claim a headache suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Jeevan felt embarrassed and low about failing, and was tempted to avoid the group.

qa.q: What makes the group's promise work for Jeevan?
qa.a: Knowing Dhruv and Ketan expect Jeevan, even joking that they would come round, keeps Jeevan turning up when motivation dips.

qa.q: How do Dhruv and Ketan seem to feel when Jeevan finds the dividing mistake?
qa.a: They seem pleased, and Dhruv grins, because the explaining did its job and exposed the gap.

grounding: A dialogue shows a study group where explaining exposes a student's gap and the promise to show up keeps Jeevan attending.
